item.title: Log-concavity of rank and crank statistics for integer partitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.17357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M(m,n)$ and $N(m,n)$ denote the numbers of partitions of $n$ with crank $m$ and rank $m$, respectively. Ji and Zang [Adv. Math. 2021] conjectured that $M(m,n)$ is log-concave in $m$ for $n\ge72$ and $|m|\le n-72$, and that $N(m,n)$ is log-concave in $m$ for $n\ge73$ and $|m|\le n-73$. In this paper, we prove these two conjectures.
item.dc:creator: Jianxi Mao, Wenle Shi

item.title: Automatic $n$-dimensional recurrences over finite $p$-groups with negative predecessor coordinates
item.description: arXiv:2611.17358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study $n$-dimensional recurrences on $\mathbb{N}^n$ over finite $p$-groups. The rules are ordered products of group endomorphisms, with a $p$-automatic additional sequence and compatible $p$-automatic boundary data. For finite, nonempty, lexicographically positive predecessor sets, we prove automaticity whenever at most one coordinate contains entries of both signs. This covers all such systems for $n=1$ and $n=2$. For $n\ge3$, lexicographic positivity alone is insufficient: a fixed three-dimensional recurrence with a single nonzero boundary value is nonautomatic in base $p$ for every prime $p$. For nonnegative predecessors, we give a direct automaton construction and explicit state bounds in the abelian case. Negative coordinates are treated using algebraic power-series division, lifting modulo prime powers, central subgroups and boundary-preserving coordinate changes. A two-parameter family with a specified rule and a single boundary seed admits an exact automaticity criterion modulo prime powers. We also give nonabelian examples and finite computational certificates, including a proof of a previously proposed formula counting nonzero Delannoy residues modulo $27$.
item.dc:creator: Bogdan Dumitru, Mihai Prunescu

item.title: Positive Dual Certificates for Real Separated Subset Sums: Chamber Optimality of the Conway-Guy and Bohman Sets, and Exact Values up to Eight
item.description: arXiv:2611.17360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f_R(n)$ be the least possible largest element of a set of $n$ positive reals whose $2^n$ subset sums are pairwise at least 1 apart, and let $f_Z(n) \ge f_R(n)$ be the corresponding integer quantity of the Erd\H{o}s distinct subset sums problem. Fixing the signs of all signed relations $\varepsilon\cdot x$, $\varepsilon \in \{-1,0,1\}^n$, decomposes the real problem into polyhedral chambers, on each of which it is a linear program. We prove that for every $n$ the Conway-Guy set is the unique optimum of its chamber. The proof is an explicit positive dual certificate consisting of $n$ signed relations that are tight at the Conway-Guy set and unit lower triangular in gap coordinates; the relations are described by blocks of consecutive coordinates together with the positions $n - k(k+1)/2$, and tightness reduces to an identity of the Conway-Guy sequence proved by induction. We then show, by a branch-and-bound over chambers in which every leaf carries an exact rational certificate, that $f_R(n) = f_Z(n)$ for all $n \le 8$; in particular $f_R(7) = 44$ and $f_R(8) = 84$. We then prove the same for both of Bohman's families, which first improve on Conway-Guy at $n = 12$ ($1159 < 1164$): every Bohman set is the unique optimum of its chamber, with a block-triangular certificate given by explicit formulas. Finally we exhibit chambers whose optimal vertex is not an integer point.
item.dc:creator: Esther Notik

item.title: A $19/5$ lower bound for the four-dimensional Erd\H{o}s box problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.17378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every power $q\ge2$ of~$2$, we construct a box-free subset of $[q^5]^4$ with $q^{19}$ points, improving the lower-bound exponent in the four-dimensional Erd\H{o}s box problem from $15/4$ to $19/5$. In fact, $[q^5]^4$ partitions into $q$ isomorphic box-free sets. The proof uses a finite-field rectangle lemma and orthogonality in a four-dimensional bilinear space. We also deduce a uniform bound $f_4(n)\ge2^{-19/20}n^{19/5}$ and a lower bound for grid-coloring numbers.
item.dc:creator: Dean Matthew Menezes

item.title: $A_1^{(1)}$-Grounded partitions at levels $1$ and $2$, Part II: affine crystal structure
item.description: arXiv:2611.17443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Grounded partitions are coloured partitions with difference conditions, introduced by Dousse and Konan, that are in bijection with the paths of the Kyoto path model of Kang, Kashiwara, Misra, Miwa, Nakashima and Nakayashiki. We describe the affine crystal structure on the grounded partitions arising from the level $1$ and level $2$ perfect crystals of type $A_1^{(1)}$. At level $1$, grounded partitions are naturally identified with $2$-restricted partitions, and the affine crystal structure is given by Kleshchev's modular branching rule for symmetric groups in characteristic $2$. At level $2$, we give explicit bracketing rules which make grounded partitions into affine crystal graphs of highest weights $2\Lambda_0$, $\Lambda_0+\Lambda_1$, and $2\Lambda_1$. We prove this by constructing explicit graph isomorphisms with the asymptotic model of Ariki and Mathas, whose vertices are Kleshchev multipartitions arising from Ariki-Koike algebras. Finally, we erase the $0$-arrows, which leaves the crystal graphs of the restrictions to the Levi subalgebra, and decompose them into finite strings. This decomposition gives new $q$-series identities at levels $1$ and $2$.
item.dc:creator: Benedek Dombos, Jihyeug Jang

item.title: Dimension bounds for higher Bruhat orders
item.description: arXiv:2611.17465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Dushnik-Miller dimension of higher Bruhat orders. For the inclusion order $B_{\mathrm{inc}}(n,k)$, with $k$ fixed, we prove that the order of dimension growth is $n^k$, by exhibiting standard examples for the lower bound and explicit systems of coordinates for the upper bound. A recent Tur\'an-system construction of Gao, Kuang, Pikhurko and Wang gives an upper coefficient within a factor smaller than $4$ of the lower coefficient. For the genuine higher Bruhat order $B(n,k)$, we construct for every fixed $k\ge3$ a standard example of order $n^{2k+1}$. We leave it open whether a polynomial upper bound on this dimension exists.
item.dc:creator: Daria Poliakova

item.title: Isolation of $k$-cliques in uniform hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.17489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A copy of a hypergraph $F$ is called an $F$-copy. For any integers $k$ and $r$ with $2 \leq r \leq k$, let $K_k^r$ denote the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph whose vertex set is $[k] = \{1, 2, \dots, k\}$ (that is, the edges of $K_k^r$ are the $r$-element subsets of $[k]$). Given an $r$-uniform $m$-edge hypergraph $H$, the $K_k^r$-isolation number of $H$, denoted by $\iota(H, K_k^r)$, is the size of a smallest subset $D$ of the vertex set of $H$ such that the closed neighbourhood $N[D]$ of $D$ intersects the vertex sets of the $K_k^r$-copies contained by $H$ (equivalently, $H-N[D]$ contains no $K_k^r$-copy). We prove that if $H$ is connected and not a $K_k^r$-copy, then $$\iota(H, K^r_k) \le \left \lfloor \frac{(r-1)m + 1}{(r-1)(\binom{k}{r}+1) + 1} \right \rfloor.$$ The bound is best possible. This is a solution to a problem of Li, Zhang and Ye. We also provide an alternative proof for $r < k$. Both proofs introduce new ideas for establishing bounds on isolation parameters.
item.dc:creator: Mattea Baluci, Peter Borg

item.title: New Congruences for Simultaneously $l$-Regular and $t$-Distinct Partition in $k$-Colors
item.dc:creator: Anjelin Mariya Johnson, S. N. Fathima

item.title: The Ulam sequence grows subexponentially
item.description: arXiv:2611.17584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the $n$-th element of the Ulam sequence, a somewhat mysterious recursively-defined sequence of positive integers, has size $e^{O(\sqrt{n})}$; previous upper bounds were exponential in $n$. Our argument uses an additive-combinatorial lemma, possibly of independent interest, about covering finite difference sets with multiplicatively short intervals. The proofs are due to ChatGPT.
item.dc:creator: Noah Kravitz

item.title: Schreier Sets And the Product of Fibonacci And Catalan Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.17657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: First, we introduce strictly super-Schreier sets, which provide a new combinatorial interpretation of products of Fibonacci and Catalan numbers. Second, we show that the numbers of sets in higher-order Schreier families do not satisfy any linear recurrence relation, thus answering a question in the existing literature.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Beanland, Hung Viet Chu, Carrie E. Finch-Smith

item.title: Nonexistence of a quasi-symmetric $2$-$(33,15,35)$ design
item.description: arXiv:2611.17678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is shown that there exists no quasi-symmetric $2$-$(33,15,35)$ design with intersection numbers $6$ and $9$. This is proved by considering the ternary code generated by the incidence vectors of the blocks and its dual code.
item.dc:creator: Masaaki Harada

item.title: Exponential Double and Multiple Riordan Arrays as Fiber Products
item.description: arXiv:2611.17748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A double Riordan array has nonzero entries only in positions $(n,k)$ with $n+k$ even, and its even and odd parts are Riordan arrays with the same multiplier function. We develop this observation systematically, with the emphasis on exponential double and exponential multiple Riordan arrays. Using generalized Riordan arrays with respect to a sequence $(c_n)$, we show that the double Riordan group, the exponential double Riordan group, the multiple Riordan group, and the exponential multiple Riordan group are fiber products of (generalized) Riordan groups over the Lagrange group. For exponential double and exponential multiple Riordan arrays this yields product and inverse formulas without square or $\ell$th roots, valid over any field of characteristic zero; an abelian normal subgroup with quotient the Lagrange group and a corresponding splitting; subgroups isomorphic to the Riordan group; an iterated split-extension description of the multiple groups; and a characterization of elements of finite order, including the fact that over ${\mathbb R}$ every element of finite order is an involution. We show that the $\ell$th power of the production matrix is the direct sum of the production matrices of the compressions, give an explicit formula for it in terms of partial Bell polynomials, and characterize these arrays by a shared $A$-sequence. Finally, we reverse the construction. Two Riordan arrays with a common multiplier can always be interleaved into a unique double Riordan array, and into an ordinary Riordan array exactly when their first functions satisfy one more condition. Examples include Pascal-, Catalan-, Morgan--Voyce-, and ballot-type arrays.
item.dc:creator: Tian-Xiao He

item.title: Closed formulas for the permanents of structured matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.17812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give finite formulas for permanents of structured matrices and prove polynomial bounds for their evaluation. Over any field, the permanent of a matrix of bounded rank-width can be computed from the matrix alone, answering a question of Lyaudet. In characteristic $p>0$, the bound is $p^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}$, where $k$ is the rank-width. In characteristic zero, a determinant formula treats Cauchy matrices with an added polynomial of fixed degrees in the row and column nodes. This includes polynomial perturbations of Hilbert matrices and dense Toeplitz and Hankel families. For ordered cuts we give a single determinant; in positive characteristic, rational diagonal sequences give a fixed rational generating function for the Toeplitz permanents. We also give formulas for cycle weights and hook immanants. For translation matrices we obtain signed determinant formulas and classify the supports for which the permanent is the coefficientwise absolute value of the determinant. Further formulas cover cyclic block matrices, residue supports, and bands bounded on one side.
item.dc:creator: M. Fazeel Anwar

item.title: Weighted Euler transforms, real-rootedness, and $\gamma$-positivity
item.description: arXiv:2611.17839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $a>0$ and a polynomial $F$ of degree $m$, let $H_{a,F}$ denote the weighted Euler numerator of $F$, defined as the numerator of the generating function $\sum_{k\ge0}(a)_kF(k)x^k/k!$ with denominator $(1-x)^{a+m}$. For every $a>0$, we show the following preservation result: if the numerators $H_{a,F}$ and $H_{a,G}$ have only real nonpositive zeros, then the same holds for $H_{a,FG}$. The proof relies on an explicit multiplication formula in falling-factorial coordinates and a characterization of multiplier sequences for generalized Laguerre bases due to Br\"and\'en and Ottergren. Furthermore, when the symmetric degrees coincide with the ordinary degrees of the input polynomials, the same operation preserves $\gamma$-positivity. For positive integers $a=r$, the weight is the Ehrhart polynomial of the standard simplex $\Delta_{r-1}$. This yields geometric preservation theorems for products with a single simplex factor, as well as applications to Gorenstein polytopes and a Reeve tetrahedron example.
item.dc:creator: Yinuo Cheng, Guoce Xin

item.title: On configurations that are nearly generalised polygons
item.description: arXiv:2611.17855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Payne (1972) introduced nearly generalised $n$-gons as $(s+1)$-regular bipartite graphs of girth $2n$ with small excess over the Moore bound. Biggs and Ito (1980) proved nonexistence of such graphs if $s > 1$ and $n > 3$, leaving open the existence of regular antipodal planes. We revisit this problem from several equivalent viewpoints. First we show that a regular antipodal plane of order $s$ is equivalent to a balanced weighing matrix whose support is the incidence matrix of a biplane with parameters \[ 2-\left(\frac{s^2+s+2}{2},\,s+1,\,2\right). \] This gives short determinant and local-arithmetic obstructions to existence. We then formulate the question of signing a biplane as an affine linear system over $\mathbb F_2$, and use this formulation to prove that no regular antipodal plane of order $s$ exists with $4\le s\le 14$. Finally, we give further equivalent formulations in terms of sharply deranged families of permutations and mutually orthogonal array-bic squares. These translations provide new computational and structural approaches to Payne's conjecture that regular antipodal planes exist only for $s=2,3$.
item.dc:creator: Sam Adriaensen, John Bamberg, Jason Williford

item.title: Goodman-type lower bounds for graph homomorphism densities
item.description: arXiv:2611.17885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite graph $H$ with $v(H)$ vertices, chromatic number $\chi(H)$, and chromatic polynomial $P_H$, define $\Phi_H(p)=(1-p)^{v(H)}P_H((1-p)^{-1})$. This polynomial interpolates the homomorphism densities of $H$ in balanced complete multipartite graphons. We study the lower bound $t(H,W)\ge\Phi_H(p)$ on the homomorphism density of $H$ in graphons $W$ of edge density $p>1-1/(\chi(H)-1)$, which generalises Goodman's triangle bound. We prove the inequality for chordal graphs whose maximal cliques have equal size, for trivially perfect graphs, and for joins of a clique and an odd cycle. The proofs use entropy along clique trees and a convexity criterion for adding a universal vertex. We also prove that a nonbipartite graph satisfies the inequality at all sufficiently high edge densities if and only if its girth is odd. For a graph on $n$ vertices whose girth is odd, the bound holds whenever $p>1-(72n^{12})^{-1}$. The proof combines Whitney's forest expansion with a spectral comparison of cycle densities. Finally, among the $117$ nonbipartite graphs on at most six vertices with no isolated vertices or isolated edges, exactly $94$ satisfy the bound. The main results are formally verified in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Taeyoung Kim

item.title: Additive cubes are avoidable over $\{0,1,2,3\}$, $\{0,1,4\}$ and $\{0,2,5\}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.17999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that additive cubes are avoidable over the alphabet $\{0,1,2,3\}$, thereby solving a long-standing question initiated by Pirillo and Varricchio in 1994. By extending the reduction and spectral machinery of Cassaigne, Currie, Schaeffer, and Shallit (2014), we prove that the search for additive cubes in such morphic images reduces to a finite graph traversal. We exhibit eight explicit morphisms from $\{0,1,3,4\}^*$ to $\{0,1,2,3\}^*$ of length 3 whose images on the Cassaigne \textit{et al.} infinite word contain no additive cubes.
item.dc:creator: Damien Jamet, Matthieu Rosenfeld

item.title: Perfect Matching Complexes of $3\times 2n$ Grid Graph
item.description: arXiv:2611.18058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The perfect matching complex of a simple graph $G$ is an abstract simplicial complex whose facets (maximal faces) are precisely the perfect matchings of $G$. In this article, we study the topology of the perfect matching complex of the $3\times 2n$ grid graph and show that it is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of $f_{n-1}$ copies of $(n-1)$-dimensional spheres, where $f_{k}$ denotes the $k$-th Fibonacci number. This proves a particular case of the conjecture given by Chandrakar and Singh for perfect matching complex of grid graphs.
item.dc:creator: Himanshu Chandrakar, Trung Chau, Shuchita Goyal, Rahul Karki, B. Subhash

item.title: Compatible zero-sum partitions of finite Abelian groups and their applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.18059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(\Gamma,+)$ be a finite Abelian group and let $g\in\Gamma\setminus\{0\}$. A partition of $\Gamma$ is called $g$-compatible if no part contains both $x$ and $x+g$. For a prescribed involution $h$ and odd $r\ge3$, we prove that $\Gamma$ admits an $h$-compatible partition into zero-sum $r$-element sets if and only if $r$ divides $|\Gamma|$ and $\Gamma$ has at least three involutions. Moreover, the partition can be chosen so that the multigraph whose vertices are its parts and whose edges are the pairs $\{x,x+h\}$ is Hamiltonian and has a proper edge coloring with $r$ colors. We also give examples, for groups of odd order and for even block sizes, in which zero-sum partitions exist but compatible ones do not. We give two applications of these partitions. For block size three, we obtain complete mappings whose cycles are precisely the parts of the partition. We also construct Hamiltonian $r$-regular $\Gamma$-distance-magic graphs admitting $0$ and every involution of $\Gamma$ as magic constants.
item.dc:creator: Ahmet Batal, Sylwia Cichacz

item.title: Upper bounds for the number of spanning forests of a graph
item.description: arXiv:2611.18076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices, and let $F(G)$ denote the number of spanning forests of $G$. Bencs and Csikv\'ari proved that every $r$-regular graph $G$ with $r\ge 2$ satisfies $F(G)\le r^n$. Motivated by this result, they conjectured that if $G$ has minimum degree at least $3$, then $F(G)\leq \prod_{i=1}^n d_i$, where $(d_1, d_2, \dots, d_n)$ is the degree sequence of $G$. In this paper, we prove that graphs with minimum degree at least $n/3$ $(n\geq7)$ satisfy $F(G)\leq \prod_{i=1}^n d_i$. We also construct a counterexample to the conjecture. We therefore further study the enumeration of spanning forests in general graphs, proving an upper bound in terms of the degree sequence and characterizing the extremal graphs attaining this bound. In addition, using the matrix-forest theorem, we obtain an upper bound for the number of spanning forests of a connected graph in terms of its algebraic connectivity, and characterize the extremal graphs attaining this bound.
item.dc:creator: Tingzeng Wu, Shuxin Lu, Xiangshuai Dong

item.title: On the Construction of New Families of Distance Equienergetic Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.18134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $G$ with vertex set $V(G)=\{v_{i}:1\leq i \leq p\}$ and edge set $E(G)=\{e_{j}:1\leq j \leq q\},$ its subdivision graph $S_G$ is generalized to $S_{G}(n,m),$ by replacing each vertex $v_{i}$ with $n$ vertices and each edge-vertex $e_{j}$ with $m$ vertices, with each copy having the same neighbors as the vertex it replaces. Building on this construction, we define the generalized subdivision vertex join $S_{G_{1}}(n,m)\dot{\vee} G_{2}$ and the generalized subdivision edge join $S_{G}(n,m)\veebar G_{2},$ which extend the known subdivision vertex and subdivision edge join of graphs. In this paper, we determine the distance spectrum of $S_{G_{1}}(n,n)\dot{\vee} G_{2}$ and $S_{G}(n,n)\veebar G_{2},$ when $G_{1}$ and $G_{2}$ are regular graphs. As an application, we construct new families of $D$-cospectral graphs and $D$-equienergetic graphs of diameter $4.$
item.dc:creator: Anjitha Ashokan, Chithra A V

item.title: Graphs attaining Haemers' toughness bound
item.description: arXiv:2611.18193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Haemers \cite{Haemers2020} conjectured that every connected noncomplete graph $G$ satisfies $t(G)\geqslant\mu_2/(\mu_n-\delta)$, where $t(G)$ is the toughness of $G$, $\mu_2$ and $\mu_n$ are its algebraic connectivity and Laplacian spectral radius, and $\delta$ is its minimum degree. Greaves and Zhu \cite{GreavesZhu2026} recently proved this conjecture, leaving the equality case open. We characterize all graphs attaining equality: a graph attains equality if and only if its complement has a complete component whose order is at least the Laplacian spectral radius of every other component. Equivalently, its algebraic connectivity and independence number sum to its order. We also determine all vertex cuts attaining the toughness, and show that for regular graphs, the equality graphs are exactly the complete multipartite graphs with parts of equal size.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Li, Cheng Yeaw Ku

item.title: The M\"obius function of factorizations with a simple prime factor
item.description: arXiv:2611.18194v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The poset of factorizations of a positive integer $n$ (ordered by refinement) is known to have a very irregular M\"obius function. We prove that this function becomes completely explicit whenever $n$ is divisible by a prime $q$ to the first power only ($q^2 \nmid n$). Specifically, between a factorization with $k$ factors and $n$ itself, the M\"obius function is given by $(-1)^{k-1}$ multiplied by the number of ways to order the factors that are not divisible by $q$. As a consequence, the sum of the absolute values of the M\"obius function over this interval equals twice the number of ordered factorizations of $n/q$.
item.dc:creator: Madjid Mirzavaziri, Daniel Yaqubi

item.title: From Butson Hadamard switching to graph switching and back
item.description: arXiv:2611.18296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Switching is a local operation that preserves specified properties of a combinatorial object. It has been used to derive constructions of inequivalent Hadamard matrices and nonisomorphic cospectral graphs. In this paper we investigate the relation between these constructions for real and Butson Hadamard matrices. We show that, while equivalent matrices have isomorphic associated graphs, the converse can fail for Butson matrices. We prove that a character decomposition determines the graph spectrum from the singular values of entrywise powers. For prime phase, we also observe that the spectrum depends only on the order and phase; for composite phase, a switching preserving the Butson property can change it. We show that Orrick's closed-quadruple and Hall-set switchings correspond to Wang-Qiu-Hu switching, up to graph isomorphism. Going in the other direction, we characterise when the Godsil-McKay and Wang-Qiu-Hu reflections preserve the Butson property and give phase-multiplicity conditions for the corresponding graph switchings. Finally we also relate block switching to cyclic graph switching under a phase-balance condition, automatic at prime phase. These results provide a basis for transferring tools and techniques between matrix switching and graph switching.
item.dc:creator: Aida Abiad, Ronan Egan, Stef Mohnen

item.title: Enumeration of Cospectral Graphs with Respect to the Average Flow Matrix
item.description: arXiv:2611.18344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph is said to be determined by the spectrum of a graph-associated matrix if no nonisomorphic graph shares the same spectrum with it. In this paper, we introduce the average flow matrix of a connected graph and study its spectral properties. We investigate its effectiveness in distinguishing graphs by carrying out a computational enumeration of connected graphs having a cospectral mate with respect to this matrix up to order 10. Our computations show that every connected graph on at most 10 vertices is determined by the spectrum of the average flow matrix. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first graph-associated matrix for which the spectrum distinguishes all connected graphs of order at most 10.
item.dc:creator: Usama Waheed, Naveed Ahmed Azam

item.title: From Diagonal Coloring to Proper Vertex Labelings Distinguishing Adjacent Facial Sums
item.description: arXiv:2611.18384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study proper vertex labelings of 3-connected plane graphs that give distinct boundary-vertex sums to faces sharing an edge. Let $\lambda(G)$ be the least $k$ for which labels from $\{0,\ldots,k\}$ suffice, and let $\laml(G)$ be its arbitrary-real-list counterpart. Our two main results are an eight-element list theorem for fullerenes and the universal bound $\lambda(G)\le708587$ for all 3-connected plane graphs. We establish structural nine- and eight-color bounds, classify triangulations whose vertices of degree at least five form an independent set, and determine their exact diagonal chromatic numbers. We also prove closure under triangular sums for $q\ge7$ diagonal colors, with an optimal uniform threshold. For cubic 3-connected plane graphs we obtain $\lambda\le14$, improving to $\lambda\le9$ in the bipartite case.
item.dc:creator: Zhou Guofei

item.title: Efficient Reconfiguration of Independent Transversals
item.description: arXiv:2611.18474v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the reconfiguration of independent transversals in graphs with a prescribed vertex partition. Given a graph $G$ with a vertex partition $\mathcal{V}=(V_1,\ldots,V_m)$, an independent transversal is an independent set containing exactly one vertex from each part $V_i$ of $\mathcal{V}$. The reconfiguration problem concerns transforming one independent transversal into another through a sequence of local changes, while preserving the independent transversal property at every step. For any fixed $r\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\epsilon>0$, we present a polynomial-time algorithm that, given an $r$-claw-free graph $G$ with a vertex partition $\mathcal{V}=(V_1,\ldots,V_m)$ and two independent transversals $S$ and $R$, either finds a polynomial-length reconfiguration path between $S$ and $R$, or identifies a nonempty set of partition classes $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathcal{V}$ such that the subgraph induced by their union admits a strong dominating set of size at most $(2+\epsilon)|\mathcal{B}|$. Our result provides an algorithmic counterpart to recent connectivity results for the reconfiguration graph of all independent transversals, and establishes polynomial bounds on its diameter under suitable conditions. As a specific application, we obtain a polynomial-time algorithm for reconfiguring perfect matchings in $r$-uniform bipartite hypergraphs $H=(A,B,E)$, that either produces a polynomial-length reconfiguration path between two given perfect matchings or identifies a subset $S\subseteq A$ whose link hypergraph $E_S$ in $B$ has a small cover.
item.dc:creator: Sahab Hajebi, Penny Haxell

item.title: Cohen Macaulayness and Buchsbaumness of Cartesian Products of Paths and Cycles
item.description: arXiv:2611.18495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the independence complexes of Cartesian products of paths and cycles. Let G(m,n) denote the Cartesian product of the path P_m and the cycle C_n, and let Delta(m,n) denote its independence complex. We determine the well-covered graphs in this family and use reduced homology to study their Cohen-Macaulay and Buchsbaum properties. Using these results, we completely classify the Cohen-Macaulay members. We then study the Buchsbaum property of Delta(m,n) through vertex links. For the remaining family P_m x C_3, we introduce an auxiliary family of graphs and use an inductive link argument together with Reisner's criterion to determine precisely when the independence complex of P_m x C_3 is Buchsbaum. Combining this with the remaining well-covered cases yields the complete Buchsbaum classification.
item.dc:creator: Bidwan Chakraborty

item.title: Polytopal realization of double root free subword complexes
item.description: arXiv:2611.18518v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a convex geometric sufficient condition for a convex polytope to realize a spherical subword complex. Using this criterion, we first prove that each root independent spherical subword complex is polytopal, for any Coxeter group. Then we prove the polytopality of double root free subword complexes, for any Coxeter groups. To prove this, we construct a polytope in an auxiliary vector space whose image under a natural affine map is the usual brick polytope. In the complex Kac-Moody case, the polytope is integral, with vertices in the character lattice of the torus of unfolded galleries in a thick building. In finite Lie types, in double root free cases, these tori are precisely the corresponding braid varieties.
item.dc:creator: Zijun Li

item.title: Many more odd zeta values are irrational
item.description: arXiv:2611.16156v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that for any sufficiently large odd integer $s$, there exist at least \[ 2.78 \, \sqrt{\frac{s \log\log s}{\log s}} \] irrational values among $\zeta(3), \zeta(5), \dots, \zeta(s)$, where $\zeta$ is the Riemann zeta function. This improves on the best known estimate by a constant factor times $\sqrt{ \log\log s}$. The proof combines the elimination technique and an arithmetic lemma of Fischler--Sprang--Zudilin, the hypergeometric constructions of Lai--Yu, and the Hankel determinant method that appeared in the proof that $\zeta(5)$ is irrational posted by Fauzan on September 17, 2026.
item.dc:creator: St\'ephane Fischler, Li Lai, Johannes Sprang, Wadim Zudilin

item.title: TSP instances that require exponentially many subtour elimination constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.17386v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct pathological TSP instances that require exponentially many subtour elimination constraints (SECs) in the sense that, if a smaller collection of SECs is imposed, then the Dantzig-Fulkerson-Johnson model returns a disconnected solution costing less than an optimal tour. For asymmetric instances on $n$ vertices, we prove a growth rate of \(\Omega(\phi^n)\), where \(\phi\approx 1.618\) is the golden ratio. A node-splitting reduction gives metric instances with \(\Omega(\phi^{n/2})\) growth. We also give instances in the plane under the Euclidean, Rectilinear, and Maximum metrics that require exponentially many SECs. Concorde struggles on them, with solve times growing exponentially despite tiny integrality gaps.
item.dc:creator: Eleonora Vercesi, Austin Buchanan

item.title: Generalized Power Graph of a Group
item.description: arXiv:2611.17525v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of graphs, called generalized power graphs, and investigate some of their key properties, such as completeness, connectivity, and planarity.
item.dc:creator: Danilo Silveira, Yerko Contreras-Rojas

item.title: A proof of the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture by embedding nilspaces in nilmanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.17567v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every compact finite-rank nilspace admits a continuous injective morphism into a toral nilspace of the same step, and hence into a connected filtered nilmanifold. Combining this embedding theorem with the general nilspace inverse theorem, we establish the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture and extend its conclusion to second-countable compact abelian groups. This yields an inverse theorem for Gowers norms on all such groups, in which the correlating functions factor through morphisms into nilmanifolds. The proof relies on substantial foundations developed in nilspace theory over the past decade, particularly the general nilspace inverse theorem and the representation of compact finite-rank nilspaces as quotients of free nilspaces.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Candela, Diego Gonz\'alez-S\'anchez, Bal\'azs Szegedy

item.title: The Exact Stabilization Time of Self-Stabilizing Coloring: Mean, Variance, and Distribution
item.description: arXiv:2611.17989v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The worst-case stabilization time of a self-stabilizing algorithm usually says little about its typical behavior beyond the order of magnitude. This paper revisits the classical self-stabilizing $Delta+1$ coloring algorithm with vertices activated at random, one at a time (the random central daemon). Considering the number of color changes as a random variable, we study its mean, variance and, on several families of graphs, its exact distribution. The analysis rests on a reduction: a vertex changes color, at most once, exactly when it is not a local maximum of a uniformly random labeling of the vertices, maxima being taken among the neighbors that share its initial color (the monochrome initial configuration is the slowest case). What can be predicted depends on what is known of the graph. The degree distribution (the view at distance one) gives the mean. The variance needs the view at distance two, in particular the triangles, and the full law needs the whole graph. We give closed-form results, from monochrome and from uniformly random initial configurations, on paths, cycles, random trees, Erd\H{o}s-R{\'e}nyi graphs and bipartite random graphs. From a monochrome start, the mean stays within a factor two of the worst case, whereas the variance ranges from zero (disjoint cliques) to order $n^2$ (the star on $n$ vertices)..
item.dc:creator: {\'E}lie de Panafieu (NPA), Fabien Mathieu (NPA), Maria Gradinariu Potop-Butucaru (NPA), S{\'e}bastien Tixeuil (NPA, IUF)

item.title: Cover times of random recursive trees and linear preferential attachment trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.18353v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the cover times of uniform random recursive trees and linear preferential attachment trees, including the negative-parameter models corresponding to random $d$-ary increasing trees. We prove explicit limits in probability and expectation when the cover times are rescaled by $n (\log n)^2$. In particular, for the uniform random recursive tree the cover time is close to $e n (\log n)^2$ with high probability.
item.dc:creator: Omer Angel, Christina Goldschmidt, Peleg Michaeli

item.title: Quadratic APN Functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^{10}$ with a Self-Equivalence of Prime Order
item.description: arXiv:2611.18358v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ have the lowest possible differential uniformity. The only known APN permutation in even dimension, in dimension six, is equivalent to a quadratic APN function with a nontrivial linear self-equivalence; no APN permutation is known for even $n \geq 8$. In a published collection of about 3.8 million quadratic APN classes of dimension eight, at most 0.34% have a nontrivial linear self-equivalence. In dimension ten, the 25 literature classes considered here all have one. We study all quadratic APN functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^{10}$ with such a self-equivalence, which usually confines them to a much smaller linear space. Up to conjugacy and power similarity, self-equivalences of prime order have 299 types. We settle 298 of them. Elementary lemmas exclude 280 types, and exhaustive searches confirm this for 242 of them. The other 18 types are settled by exhaustive searches with exact equivalence certificates. Up to extended affine equivalence, the 298 types contain 29 classes of quadratic APN functions, four of them new. This also classifies the quadratic APN functions with coefficients in a subfield. Exactly 24 classes contain one with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_4$, and all 3 that contain one with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_{32}$ are among them. The open type consists of the quadratic canonical triplicate functions. They correspond to maximum additive Hermitian rank-distance codes. Three different searches find only the invariants of 16 classes, all among the 29. We conjecture there are no others. No quadratic APN function in the 298 settled types is Carlet-Charpin-Zinoviev equivalent to a permutation.
item.dc:creator: Emanuele Bellini

item.title: Color Refinement Distinguishes Connected Rooted Outerplanar Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.18391v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Color refinement, also known as the $1$-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm ($1$-WL), is a classical near-linear-time heuristic for graph isomorphism, which also captures the expressive power of message-passing graph neural networks. A long line of work asks on which graph classes $1$-WL, or its higher-dimensional variant $k$-WL, identifies every graph; the least such $k$ is the WL-dimension of the class. Planar graphs have WL-dimension at most $3$ (Kiefer, Ponomarenko and Schweitzer, 2019), and whether $2$-WL already distinguishes all planar graphs is a central open problem. We bring new insight on this question for outerplanar graphs, whose WL-dimension is $2$. We show that color refinement, i.e. 1-WL, distinguishes connected rooted outerplanar graphs: two non-isomorphic such graphs receive different stable colorings once a single vertex, the root, is individualized. The root is necessary, as there are non-isomorphic $2$-connected outerplanar graphs that color refinement does not distinguish. Our result extends to pseudo-rooted graphs, in which the stable coloring merely contains a singleton color class, and to non-connected graphs whose components all contain such a class. Consequently, the $(1,1)$-WL test of Rattan and Seppelt (2023) distinguishes all outerplanar graphs. We proceed by inversion: we reconstruct a connected rooted outerplanar graph, up to isomorphism, from its color graph, the weighted quotient of the graph by its stable color classes, together with its root color. The reconstruction runs in time linear in the output size and is canonical, which yields a near-linear-time canonization algorithm for these graphs. Our main tool is a dichotomy lemma, formalized in Rocq: in a rooted outerplanar graph with an equitable coloring, every block either receives pairwise distinct colors or admits a color-preserving mirror symmetry fixing its vertex closest to the root.
item.dc:creator: Louann Coste (DI-ENS), M{\'o}nika Csik{\'o}s (IRIF), Laurent Viennot (DI-ENS, ARGO)

item.title: A quotient formula for the Behrend function
item.description: arXiv:2611.18432v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Behrend function is essential in enumerative geometry. However, computing it, even in zero dimension, has been a highly subtle and mysterious matter since its introduction in the 2000s. We present a quotient formula for the Behrend function of any closed $r$-dimensional affine scheme $X^r \subset \mathbb{A}^N$, evaluated at a singular point, where $0\leq r \leq N-1$. In particular, if the scheme is monomial, we associate parallelepipeds to it and interpret the Behrend function as simple volume information about them. The results here, in particular, recover the recent results of Graffeo-Ricolfi for the zero-dimensional case in 2D in \cite{Graffeo-Ricolfi}, and also the more recent result of Polini-Sammartan-Ulrich on the zero-dimensional case in \cite{PSU26}.
item.dc:creator: Fatemeh Rezaee

item.title: Rigidity of the moving particle lemma for the interchange process
item.description: arXiv:2611.18483v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G=(V,c)$ be a finite connected weighted graph. We establish the exact conditions for attaining equality in the moving particle lemma for the interchange process on $G$ subject to a unit voltage drop across two terminal vertices $x\neq y \in V$. First, equality can occur only in irreducible representations indexed by partitions with at most two rows. We then show that the equality phenomenon beyond the constant and linear sectors is already visible in the two-particle exclusion process. Such equality occurs in exactly two cases: either the harmonic $x$--$y$ voltage is $\frac12$ on every nonterminal vertex, and the induced nonterminal graph $G[V\setminus\{x,y\}]$ is disconnected; or the harmonic voltage is constant on each connected component of $G[V\setminus \{x,y\}]$, and both voltage values $a$ and $1-a$, with $0\le a<\frac12$, occur. In each case we compute the equality kernel in every degree and particle sector. The resulting decomposition gives the complete equality kernel for exclusion and, through the regular representation, for the interchange process.
item.dc:creator: Joe P. Chen

item.title: A Note on Decomposable and Reducible Integer Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2003.01453v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose necessary and sufficient conditions for an integer matrix to be decomposable in terms of its Hermite normal form. Specifically, to each integer matrix, we associate a symmetric integer matrix whose reducibility can be efficiently determined by elementary linear algebra techniques, and which completely determines the decomposability of the first one.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Mariju\'an, Ignacio Ojeda, Alberto Vigneron-Tenorio

item.title: Stabilities of the Kleitman diameter theorem
item.description: arXiv:2411.08325v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of subsets of $[n]$. The diameter of $\mathcal{F}$ is defined as the maximum size of the symmetric difference between any two of its members. Resolving a conjecture of Erd\H{o}s, Kleitman determined the maximum size of a family with fixed diameter. Specifically, if $2\leq s\leq n-2$ and $\mathcal{F}\subseteq2^{[n]}$ is a family with diameter $s$, then for $s=2d$, $|\mathcal{F}|\le \sum_{i=0}^d {n \choose i}$; for $s=2d+1$, $|\mathcal{F}|\le \sum_{i=0}^d {n \choose i} + {n-1 \choose d}$. This result, known as the Kleitman diameter theorem, generalizes both the Katona union theorem and the Erd\H{o}s--Ko--Rado theorem. In 2017, Frankl provided a complete characterization of the extremal families for Kleitman's theorem and established a stability result. In this paper, we determine the extremal families for Frankl's theorem and prove a further stability result of Kleitman's theorem. This solves a recent problem proposed by Li and Wu and provides the second stability for the Kleitman diameter theorem.
item.dc:creator: Yongjiang Wu, Yongtao Li, Lihua Feng, Jiuqiang Liu, Guihai Yu

item.title: Colouring signed analogues of Kneser, Schrijver, and Borsuk graphs
item.description: arXiv:2412.20001v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Kneser signed graph $\KS(n,k)$, $k\leq n$, is the graph whose vertices are signed $k$-subsets of $[n]$ (i.e. $k$-subsets $S$ of $\{ \pm 1, \pm 2, \ldots, \pm n\}$ such that $S\cap (-S)=\emptyset$). Two vertices $A$ and $B$ are adjacent with a positive edge if $A\cap (-B)=\emptyset$ and with a negative edge if $A\cap B=\emptyset$. We prove that the balanced chromatic number of $\KS(n,k)$ is $n-k+1$. We then introduce the signed analogue of Schrijver graphs and show that choosing one representative from each antipodal pair of alternating signed $k$-sets gives a vertex-critical subgraph of $\KS(n,k)$ with respect to balanced colouring. For the Borsuk signed graph on $S^d$, we obtain balanced chromatic number $d+1$ for sufficiently small distance parameter and relate this equality to antipodal covers of the sphere. On $S^2$, spherical and projective covering bounds give three, four and six as the first successive values of the balanced chromatic number.
item.dc:creator: Luis Kuffner, Reza Naserasr, Lujia Wang, Xiaowei Yu, Huan Zhou, Xuding Zhu

item.title: Branching Ratios of Input Trees for Directed Multigraphs
item.description: arXiv:2501.06812v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define the branching ratio of the input tree of a node in a finite directed multigraph, prove that it exists for every node, and show that it is equal to the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of the induced subgraph determined by all upstream nodes. This real eigenvalue exists by the Perron-Frobenius Theorem for non-negative matrices. We motivate our analysis with simple examples, obtain information about the asymptotics for the limit growth of the input tree, and establish other basic properties of the branching ratio.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Boldi, Ian Stewart

item.title: Rubik's Abstract Polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2502.13518v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We generalize the Rubik's cube, together with its group of configurations, to any abstract regular polytope. We discuss general aspects, and provide a description of the group of the Rubik's simplex in arbitrary dimension, and of Rubik's tori. We sketch an analogous argument for the Rubik's hypercube as well.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Luca Marchetti

item.title: A complete classification of perfect state transfer in Grover walks on Cayley graphs over dihedral groups
item.description: arXiv:2605.02254v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a complete classification of Cayley graphs over dihedral groups that exhibit perfect state transfer between vertex states in Grover walks. For $n\ge 3$, let $D_n:=\langle a,b : a^n=b^2=1,\ bab=a^{-1}\rangle$ be the dihedral group of order $2n$, and let $S\subseteq D_n\setminus\{1\}$ satisfying $S=S^{-1}$ and $\langle S\rangle =D_n$. We show that the Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(D_n,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if $(D_n,S)$ is equivalent to one of the following pairs: $(D_n,\{b,ba\})$; $(D_n,\{a,a^{-1},ba,ba^{-1}\})$, where $4$ does not divide $n$; or $(D_{2m},\{b,ba^{m},ba,ba^{m+1}\})$, where $m$ is odd. Our proof combines the representation theory of $D_n$ with tools from algebraic number theory.
item.dc:creator: Koushik Bhakta, Bikash Bhattacharjya, Xiwang Cao

item.title: An annihilation-number Caro-Wei bound: a TxGraffiti conjecture and an independence-number bracket
item.description: arXiv:2606.29553v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Computable independence bounds give intervals that can be compared by containment or by their worst-case endpoint ratios. For positive maximum degree $\Delta$, the Caro-Wei sum $W$ bounds the independence number from below, while $(\Delta+1)W/2$ bounds it from above. A second interval has the Havel-Hakimi residue as its lower endpoint and the annihilation number as its upper endpoint. This note proves that the annihilation number does not exceed the Caro-Wei upper endpoint. This upper bound is sharp, with equality for regular graphs of positive degree and even order. Since the residue is at least $W$, this upper bound places the residue-annihilation interval inside the Caro-Wei interval. Both endpoints can improve strictly on one graph, although the sharp worst-case endpoint ratio remains unchanged, even for connected graphs. The annihilation-number bound also proves a conjectured lower estimate based on the annihilation number and residue for every connected graph with at least three vertices. Equality in this estimate holds for exactly eight graph types, while the single edge violates it. For maximum degree at least three, however, the estimate never exceeds the residue, even without connectedness.
item.dc:creator: Chakshu Gupta

item.title: Tree-partitions of graphs with bounded tree-depth
item.description: arXiv:2608.12723v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A tree-partition of a graph $G$ is a partition of $V(G)$ such that identifying the vertices in each part gives a tree. It is known that every graph with treewidth $k$ and maximum degree $\Delta(G)$ has a tree-partition in which each part has size $O(k\cdot\Delta(G))$. In this paper, we study tree-partitions of graphs with bounded tree-depth, a stronger parameter than treewidth, with an additional property for the tree $T$ indexing the tree-partition. We prove that every connected graph with tree-depth $h$ admits a $T$-partition for some tree $T$ with $\operatorname{rad}(T)\leq h-1$ and with width at most $\mathrm{max}\{1, (4h-10)\Delta(G)+1\}$.
item.dc:creator: Rong Chen, Huayue Liu

item.title: Order dimension beyond rank for simplicial hyperplane arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2608.14092v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the order dimension of the poset of regions in a simplicial hyperplane arrangement can exceed its rank, answering a question of Reading and Segovia. Examples are Coxeter arrangements $H_4$ and $E_6$, with $\dim W(H_4) \geq 5$ and $\dim W(E_6) \geq 7$.
item.dc:creator: Daria Poliakova

item.title: The Brualdi--Hoffman--Tur\'{a}n problem for odd wheels: Resolving a conjecture of Yu, Li and Peng
item.description: arXiv:2608.16127v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper addresses the Brualdi--Hoffman--Tur\'{a}n problem, which asks for the maximum adjacency spectral radius over graphs with a fixed number of edges that forbid a prescribed subgraph. We settle an open conjecture due to Yu, Li and Peng for odd wheel graphs $W_{2k+1}$. A striking dichotomy appears in the extremal configurations: the forbidden-$W_5$ case and the general case $k\ge 3$ rely on identical stability and dense-core reductions but produce completely different extremal graphs. For sufficiently large size $m$, we derive sharp spectral inequalities and give complete characterizations for graphs achieving equality. Our approach combines the edge-spectral stability theorem with the dense-core method and residual-function analysis. Beyond solving the target conjecture, the developed framework provides a systematic approach for edge-spectral Tur\'{a}n problems and implies several known results for odd cycles, friendship graphs and odd fans. Directions for future research on edge-spectral supersaturation are also discussed.
item.dc:creator: Longfei Fang, Mingqing Zhai, Yuhan Zhang

item.title: VC-dimension of distance graphs in finite field geometries
item.description: arXiv:2609.32052v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the VC-dimension of distance graphs of large subsets of vector spaces over finite fields. For $3\leq k\leq d$, we prove the distance graph of $E\subset \F_q^d$ has VC-dimension at least $k$ provided that $|E|>Cq^{\min(d-1,\frac{d+k-1}{2})}$. We also show that this exponent is sharp in the $k=d$ case.
item.dc:creator: Brian McDonald Bakas, Moustapha Diallo, Alex McDonald

item.title: Prescribed-Vertex Rainbow Cycle Spectra in Graph Systems under a Local Ore Condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.24427v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\GraphSys=(G_1,\ldots,G_n)$ be a system of graphs on a common $n$-vertex set, put $\delta(v)=\min_i d_{G_i}(v)$ and $E_\cap=\bigcap_i E(G_i)$, and write $d^c$ for rainbow distance. Assume that each $G_i$ is $2$-connected and that $d^c(u,v)\le2$ and $\delta(u)+\delta(v)<n$ imply $uv\in E_\cap$. We prove that either every prescribed vertex belongs to a rainbow cycle of every length $4,\ldots,n$, or all members coincide with the balanced complete bipartite graph. The non-exceptional systems are also rainbow pancyclic. Under the stronger local cutoff $4n/3-1$, every vertex additionally lies on a rainbow triangle, yielding rainbow vertex-pancyclicity; the cutoff is sharp in the stated congruence class. The proofs use prescribed-color detours, root-preserving neighborhood separation, and a rigidity theorem for missing rooted lengths.
item.dc:creator: Ailian Chen, Jiahuang Lin

item.title: Counting Lattice Points in Translations: Uniqueness and Existence Results
item.description: arXiv:2610.26523v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Generalizing a recent theorem by Higashitani et al. (Comb. Theory 2025), it is shown that a convex body $K$ is uniquely described up to integer translation by the function $\mathrm{t}_K(v) = |(K-v)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n|$, $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$. For a lattice polytope $P$ the function $\mathrm{t}_P$ is decomposed into homogeneous components $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$, similar to the Ehrhart polynomial. It is shown that the functions $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$ are simultaneous eigenfunctions of a family of linear operators introduced by Kubert and Lang in (Math. Z. 1976) and that, conversely, the linear spaces of piecewise constant eigenfunctions are generated by the respective coefficients $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$. A structure theorem for the simultaneous eigenspace corresponding to the $(n-1)$st coefficient in the decomposition of $\mathrm{t}_P$ is obtained. This leads to an explicit description of the set of functions $\mathrm{t}_P$, where $P$ ranges over all lattice polygons, as well as to inequalities for the number of lattice points in dilated and translated lattice polytopes.
item.dc:creator: Ansgar Freyer, Georg C. Hofst\"atter

item.title: Two q-Deformations of Narayana Polynomials: Rogers Moments, Hankel Positivity, and q-Narayana Kernels
item.description: arXiv:2610.28691v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study two $q$-deformations of the continuous interpolation between type $B$ and shifted type $A$ Narayana polynomials, both based on the continuous $q$-ultraspherical (Rogers) functional. For the affine-moment deformation, we establish coefficientwise Hankel total positivity via a continuant criterion and determine Hankel determinants and extremal coefficients of minors. The Askey--Wilson basis deformation yields a basic-hypergeometric Narayana kernel whose row polynomials have simple negative zeros, strict interlacing, and $\gamma$-positivity after palindromic normalization. A $q^2$-Askey--Wilson integral gives a continuous-parameter moment proof of the Krattenthaler--Wachs super $q$-Narayana expansion; an ordinary-power expansion recovers Pan's Touchard identity. For $0<q<1$ and $\theta>-1$, we establish total positivity of the kernel triangle and strict total positivity of its associated square, extending Wang--Yang's results simultaneously in $(\theta,q)$. We also prove coefficientwise total nonnegativity through order two for endpoint triangles and give an exact triangular change of basis between the deformations. Finally, we identify Tevlin's dual super $q$-Narayana polynomials with a normalized kernel, derive the recurrence for their index-two $q$-$\gamma$ coefficients via Rogers-functional Pearson--Christoffel identities, and deduce total positivity of the dual triangles and strict total positivity of their squares.
item.dc:creator: Jiang Zeng

item.title: Explicit strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs using a new graph parameter
item.description: arXiv:2610.33219v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A strong blocking set is a set of points in a finite projective space that intersects every hyperplane of the space in a spanning set of the hyperplane. These objects have been studied both in finite geometry and coding theory due to their equivalence with minimal codes. We give an explicit construction of strong blocking sets using expander graphs that improves the explicit construction of Alon et al. (Noga Alon, Anurag Bishnoi, Shagnik Das, Alessandro Neri, Strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs. Transactions of the American Mathematical Society ) by introducing a new geometrically motivated graph parameter that is better suited for this problem. Using this approach, we improve the constant $C$ in the explicit construction of a strong blocking set of size $C (q+1) k$ in the $(k - 1)$-dimensional projective space over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q \geq 7$.
item.dc:creator: Anurag Bishnoi, Ioannis Kakatelis

item.title: Short permutation pattern waves: The complete length-five classification
item.description: arXiv:2611.04184v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a permutation pi in Sk, a pi-wave is an increasing sequence of integers whose consecutive gaps have relative order pi. Let g(pi, n) be the maximum cardinality of a pi-wave-free subset of [n], and let P(pi, r) be the least integer N such that every r-coloring of [N] contains a monochromatic pi-wave. We determine the asymptotic orders of both functions for every permutation of length at most five. Existing upper bounds and weak-wave constructions provide sharp bounds for all but eight length-five patterns in S_5. For these eight exceptional alternating patterns, we establish g(pi, n) = Theta((log n)squared) and P(pi, r) = Theta(r(log r)squared).
item.dc:creator: Lihong Qiu, Minglei Mao, Yaping Mao

item.title: A Trivalent Graph of Girth 14 and Order 372
item.description: arXiv:2611.09000v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The smallest known trivalent graph of girth 14 is constructed. The graph has 372 vertices, improving the old upper bound of 384 \cite{exoo14}. The construction uses methods that may be new to this problem.
item.dc:creator: Geoffrey Exoo, Theodore Kolokolnikov

item.title: Face lattices of polytopes and bipolar polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2611.13896v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the face lattice of every convex polytope $Q$ is, on the combinatorial level, the vertex set of a polytope one dimension higher: the faces of $Q$ are the vertices of a \emph{bipolar polytope} $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$, and the intervals of the face lattice are its faces. Here a bipolar polytope is a polytope with two distinguished vertices, the poles, such that every facet contains exactly one of them and an intersection property holds. The vertices of every bipolar polytope carry a lattice order whose intervals are the faces, and this lattice is the face lattice of the vertex figure at either pole; conversely, every atomistic and coatomistic lattice that is an abstract polytope arises in this way. Geometrically, the polar of the Cayley polytope of $Q$ and $Q^\circ$ is a convex realization of $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$ whenever the normal fan and the face fan of $Q$ satisfy a certain interval condition; this holds for cubes and cross-polytopes and for suitable realizations of all polytopes of dimension at most three. Finally, every combinatorial type of $3$-polytope has a realization that decomposes into convex bipolar polytopes, one for each vertex.
item.dc:creator: Jan Pavl\'ik

item.title: Ehrhart Series and Transfer Matrices for Period-Two Polytopes with Consecutive Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2611.15122v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a family of period-two polytopes that can be naturally realized as lattice polytopes. In contrast to polytopes defined by a uniform system of inequalities, this family is characterized by consecutive coordinate inequalities whose bounds alternate between $s+1$ and $s$. The lattice points of these polytopes admit an explicit transfer-matrix formulation, which provides an effective framework for their enumeration and analysis. Furthermore, by considering fixed dilations, we investigate the associated dimensional generating functions and derive rational forms for the generating functions of the lattice points in the $m$-th dilates of the polytopes.
item.dc:creator: Yangbiao Zhou

item.title: $(r,s)$-Designs in the Nonbinary Johnson Scheme: Constructions and Linear Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.16256v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using factorizations of complete graphs, we determine the existence conditions for $(2,1)$-designs in the nonbinary Johnson scheme where each $3$-element subset appears exactly once as a support. Furthermore, by utilizing large sets of Steiner triple systems, we construct designs with index $1$ that cannot be obtained from the known construction combining block designs and orthogonal arrays. For linear codes, we express multiplicative character sums over specified nonzero coordinates as sums over the codewords of the dual code. Using this identity along with the rank of a matrix formed by Krawtchouk polynomials, we provide a sufficient condition for the set of all codewords of a given weight to form an $(r,s)$-design. In this matrix, we can utilize not only the rows corresponding to weights absent from the code, but also the rows corresponding to weights for which the set of codewords already forms a design. Moreover, let $q>2$ be a prime power, and let $0 \neq C \subsetneq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a linear code with exactly two nonzero weights. For $t \geq 2$, the set of all codewords of weight $w \geq t$ forms a non-empty $(t,t)$-design if and only if the dual minimum distance is at least $t+2$. Consequently, this provides a negative answer to the Wu--Zhou problem concerning two-weight codes with a dual minimum distance of $3$.
item.dc:creator: Ryutaro Misawa, Yuuho Tanaka

item.title: Ideals generated by corner-interval minors
item.description: arXiv:2506.09618v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we study binomial ideals generated by an arbitrary collection of corner-interval $2$-minors of a generic matrix. We determine the minimal prime ideals of such ideals and characterize their radicality in the special case of corner minors. Moreover, we discuss connectivity properties of contingency tables in algebraic statistics. We compute the Hilbert-Poincar\'e polynomial of the ideal generated by the set of all corner-interval minors and we derive the formula for the regularity in the case of corner minors.
item.dc:creator: Marie Amalore Nambi

item.title: Two Tiling is Undecidable
item.description: arXiv:2506.11628v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the following problem is undecidable: given two polygonal prototiles, determine whether the plane can be tiled with rotated and translated copies of them. This improves a result of Demaine and Langerman [SoCG 2025], who showed undecidability for three tiles. Along the way, we show that tiling with one prototile is undecidable if there can be edge-to-edge matching rules. This is the first result to show undecidability for monotiling with only local matching constraints.

item.title: On the Parameterized Complexity of Grundy Domination and Zero Forcing Problems
item.description: arXiv:2508.18104v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider two different problem families that deal with domination in graphs. On the one hand, we focus on dominating sequences. In such a sequence, every vertex dominates some vertex of the graph that was not dominated by any earlier vertex in the sequence. The problem of finding the longest dominating sequence is known as $\mathsf{Grundy~Domination}$. Depending on whether the closed or the open neighborhoods are used for domination, there are three other versions of this problem: $\mathsf{Grundy~Total~Domination}$, $\mathsf{L\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$, and $\mathsf{Z\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$. We show that all four problem variants are $\mathsf{W[1]}$-complete when parameterized by the solution size. On the other hand, we consider the family of zero forcing problems which form the parametric duals of the Grundy domination problems. In these problems, one looks for the smallest set of vertices initially colored blue such that certain color change rules are able to color all other vertices blue. It has been shown that the dual of $\mathsf{Z\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$, known as $\mathsf{Zero~Forcing~Set}$, is in $\mathsf{FPT}$ when parameterized by the treewidth or the solution size. We extend the treewidth result to the other three variants of zero forcing and their respective Grundy domination problems. Our algorithm also implies an $\mathsf{FPT}$ algorithm for $\mathsf{Grundy~Domination}$ when parameterized by the number of vertices that are not in the dominating sequence. In contrast, we show that $\mathsf{L\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$ is $\mathsf{W[1]}$-hard for that parameter.

item.title: Directed distances in bipolar-oriented triangulations: exact exponents and scaling limits
item.description: arXiv:2510.26123v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study longest and shortest directed paths in the following natural model of directed random planar maps: the uniform infinite bipolar-oriented triangulation (UIBOT), which is the local limit of uniform bipolar-oriented triangulations around a typical edge. We construct the Busemann function which measures directed distance to $\infty$ along a natural interface in the UIBOT. We show that in the case of longest (resp.\ shortest) directed paths, this Busemann function converges in the scaling limit to a $2/3$-stable L\'evy process (resp.\ a $4/3$-stable L\'evy process). We also prove up-to-constants bounds for directed distances in finite bipolar-oriented triangulations sampled from a Boltzmann distribution, and for size-$n$ cells in the UIBOT. These bounds imply that in a typical subset of the UIBOT with $n$ edges, longest directed path lengths are of order $n^{3/4}$ and shortest directed path lengths are of order $n^{3/8}$. These results give the scaling dimensions for discretizations of the (hypothetical) $\sqrt{4/3}$-directed Liouville quantum gravity metrics. The main external input in our proof is the bijection of Kenyon-Miller-Sheffield-Wilson (2015). We do not use any continuum theory. We expect that our techniques can also be applied to prove similar results for directed distances in other random planar map models and for longest increasing subsequences in pattern-avoiding permutations.

item.title: Kusner's conjecture on equilateral sets is false
item.description: arXiv:2608.14013v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We disprove Kusner's 1983 conjecture that every equilateral set in $\ell_p^n$ with $2<p<\infty$ has at most $n+1$ points: there exist $58$ points in $\mathbb{R}^{56}$ whose pairwise $\ell_5$ distances are all equal, so the maximum equilateral-set size satisfies $e(\ell_5^{56})\ge58>57$. This is the first equilateral set of more than $n+1$ points in $\ell_p^n$ for any finite $p\ge2$. The construction persists on an open interval of exponents around $5$. The configuration is specified by the unique solution of an explicit polynomial system with rational coefficients in a rational box; existence and uniqueness are proved by exact integer inequalities. The existence of the $58$-point equilateral set in $\ell_5^{56}$ has been formalised in Lean from standard axioms.

item.title: On Samuels' Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2608.18392v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $0\leq\mu_1\leq\cdots\leq\mu_n$ and let $\lambda>\sum_{i=1}^n\mu_i$. Let $X_1,...,X_n$ be independent nonnegative random variables satisfying $\mathbb{E}X_i=\mu_i$, and write $D_i := \lambda-\sum_{k=1}^{i-1}\mu_k$ for $1\leq i\leq n$. We prove that $$ \inf_{X_1,...,X_n} \mathbb{P}\left( \sum_{i=1}^nX_i<\lambda \right) = \min_{1\leq i\leq n} \prod_{j=i}^n \left( 1-\frac{\mu_j}{D_i} \right). $$ The bound is sharp and is attained. This proves Samuels' conjecture. Feige's conjecture is thereby resolved, since it follows immediately from the equal-means case. The proof is self-contained.

item.title: Tiling 3D Space by (Translates of) a Single Polycube is Undecidable
item.description: arXiv:2610.12392v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove co-RE-completeness, and thus undecidability, of the following problem: given a single (connected) polycube, decide whether it tiles 3D Euclidean space by translations. The same result holds if we also allow rotations and/or reflections. We reduce from Wang tiling using the decorated two-prime Sudoku construction of Greenfeld and Tao and a cyclic encoding adapted from OpenAI's 3D aperiodic tile, and apply a reduction of Kim to make the prototile connected (via faces). Dimension three is optimal: translational monotiling is known to be decidable in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ and for a single (possibly disconnected) polyomino in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

item.title: Upper tail large deviations of regular subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.31590v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a $\Delta$-regular connected graph $H$ we obtain the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, in the localized regime $np^{\Delta/2}\gg(\log n)^{1/(v_H-2)}$ and $p\ll 1$, where $p:=d/n$ and $v_H$ is the number of vertices in $H$, and identify the typical structure of $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ conditioned on this rare event. The degree constraint in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ changes the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi picture in two ways. First, the hub construction that competes with a clique in the regime $p \gg n^{-1/\Delta}$ is not feasible here. Consequently, for $\Delta \geq 3$ throughout the entire localized regime, both the rate function and the conditional structure are governed by a planted almost-clique, of size roughly $\delta^{1/v_H}np^{\Delta/2}$. Second, as no clique in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ can be of size greater than $(d+1)$, for $\Delta=2$ (i.e.~in case of cycles), the rate function and the conditional structure are governed by $\lfloor\delta\rfloor$ many planted almost-cliques of size roughly $d$ and another planted almost-clique of size roughly $\{\delta\}^{1/v_H}d$. For cycles of even length, in lieu of pairs of almost-cliques each of size roughly $d$, the conditional structure may possess copies of almost-bicliques with each side roughly of size $d$. In the complementary regime $1\ll n^{v_H}p^{e_H}\ll(\log n)^{\alpha^*_H/(\alpha^*_H-1)}$, where $e_H$ is the number of edges and $\alpha^*_H$ is the fractional independence number of $H$, and $H$ is a strictly balanced graph (and thus including regular $H$), we show that the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ match with those in the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi setting. In this regime, we further show that almost all unlabeled copies of $H$ conditioned on the upper tail event are edge disjoint.

item.title: Thales's theorem in higher dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.14277v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the Euclidean plane, Thales's theorem is equivalent to the statement that a quadrilateral with two opposite right angles has a circumscribed circle. We generalize the latter to higher dimensions: a convex polytope with two distinguished vertices, the \emph{poles}, such that the faces spanned by the two poles are perpendicular, is inscribed in the sphere whose diameter joins its poles. These \emph{orthogonally bipolar} polytopes are exactly the bipolar polytopes of a companion paper that arise as cutouts by orthogonal projections. As an application we show that for a polytope $P$ and a point $B$, the balls with diameters $[V,B]$, $V$ a vertex of $P$, cover $P$, and that the power diagram of their boundary spheres refines this covering to a tiling. Further, we investigate the properties of orthogonally bipolar polytopes, their characterization, and their application to tilings: in dimension three, the cutouts of $P$ by the orthogonal projections of $B$ onto its faces tile $P$ by orthogonally bipolar polytopes exactly when every such projection lies in the relative interior of its face. Finally, we propose an interpretation of the topic in political science.
